description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” on the x-axis and two performance metrics — “Perplexity” on the left y-axis and “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)” on the right y-axis — for a KV cache compression method evaluated in the PyramidInfer paper. The x-axis spans from 0 to 100% in increments of 20, with a linear scale. The left y-axis (Perplexity) ranges from 4.2 to 4.7, marked at 0.1 intervals, while the right y-axis (GPU Mem. Ratio %) spans from 40% to 100%, marked at 10% intervals. Four lines are plotted: “Perplexity” (orange, solid line with circle markers) starts at ~4.6 at 10% recent sequence ratio, drops sharply to ~4.3 at 40%, fluctuates slightly between 4.3–4.35 up to 80%, then rises to ~4.4 at 100%. “Full Cache PPL” (red, dashed line) is a horizontal reference line at ~4.38. “GPU Mem. Ratio” (blue, solid line with circle markers) increases gradually from ~42% at 10% to ~55% at 80%, then jumps sharply to ~100% at 100%. “Full Cache GPU Mem.” (blue, dashed line) is a horizontal reference line at 100%. The plot demonstrates that as the recent sequence ratio increases, GPU memory usage rises significantly only near 100%, while perplexity remains relatively stable after an initial drop.
